annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "Shaun" on page 216 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Gods (closing) phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Norris, Margot. The Decentered Universe of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/decentereduniver0000norr
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "Night" on page 216 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. During this Age of Gods (closing) phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net
